subject: Cairn Health: Minimal proof set + subprocessor access matrix for SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: Natalie Brooks <natalie@cairnhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security_ops@cairnhealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: minimal proof set + subprocessor access matrix for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking this. We're performing a SIG/CAIQ intake this week and need a compact bundle from Redwood so our vendor team can triage quickly. Can you provide a "minimal proof set" (no more than 5-7 artifacts) aligned to common SIG controls, plus a subprocessor access matrix that shows which third parties have access to customer data, the type of access, and residency? Key asks: 
- SOC 2 status (assertion + date)
- Encryption key custody (KMS owner / residency)
- Subprocessor roster + purpose + access level
- Data retention default and backup residency
- Evidence for ephemeral key rotation / tokenization (if applicable)

If possible, include file stubs we can download (PDF / CSV). Also let me know if you prefer we sign an NDA before detailed artifact delivery.

Ideal turnaround: 48 hours. We have a brief vendor call slot tomorrow 10–10:30 PT if you can do a quick 20 minute walkthrough.

Thanks,
Natalie Brooks
Sr. Vendor Risk Analyst
Cairn Health

---
Attachment: None

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Natalie Brooks <natalie@cairnhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: minimal proof set + subprocessor access matrix for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a compact bundle to speed your intake.

Proposed minimal proof set (we'll redact operational details where needed):
1) SOC 2 Type II assertion excerpt (cover page + scope) — redwood_soc2_assertion_excerpt.pdf
2) Subprocessor access matrix (CSV) — subprocessor_access_matrix_20271109.csv
3) KMS provenance summary (who holds keys, residency, rotation cadence) — kms_provenance_summary.pdf
4) Backup & retention summary (regions, default retention, encryption at rest) — backup_retention_onepager.pdf
5) Tokenization/ephemeral key notes (rotation frequency + short log sample) — token_rotation_notes.txt

I've attached a compact PDF (redwood_minimal_proofset_v1.pdf) that maps those artifacts to SIG control IDs for quicker review. If you need the full SOC 2 report, we can provide it under an NDA — the excerpt should be fine for initial triage.

Action items from our side:
- Laura: compile redactions and certify the SOC 2 excerpt + backup summary (ETA 24 hours)
- Irene: produce KMS provenance summary and a sanitized export of KMS holders (ETA 48 hours)
- Ben: validate the subprocessor CSV matches our canonical roster and add access levels (ETA 24 hours)

We can do the 10:00 PT walkthrough tomorrow — I'll set up a 20 minute invite and include a short screenshare of the files. Tell me if you prefer a signed NDA first.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_minimal_proofset_v1.pdf, subprocessor_access_matrix_20271109.csv, kms_provenance_summary.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: minimal proof set + subprocessor access matrix for SIG/CAIQ review

Adding status and delivery plan:

Connor — I'll own the SOC 2 excerpt redaction and the backup/retention one-pager. Deliverables and times:
- redwood_soc2_assertion_excerpt.pdf (cover page + scope + auditor statement) — ETA 24 hours.
- backup_retention_onepager.pdf (regions: us-west-2, us-east-1; backups encrypted with customer KMS keys (BYOK optional), default retention 90 days) — ETA 24 hours.

Irene, can you confirm whether the KMS audit export will include last-rotation timestamps for customer keys? If so, we should sanitize key IDs before we send. If not, a provenance summary (who/what service has custodial access) will do.

Ben — please do a quick QA on the subprocessor CSV and make sure the "access_level" column uses our standard three-tier labels (admin / service / read-only). If you find any transient contractors with admin rights, flag for removal before we hand this to the customer.

NDA: we typically don't require a new NDA for a SIG intake; our security intake is covered under the master MSA for documentation exchange. If Cairn requires a specific DPA or narrower NDA, let us know and legal will expedite.

Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: None (internal planning)

From: Natalie Brooks <natalie@cairnhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security_ops@cairnhealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: minimal proof set + subprocessor access matrix for SIG/CAIQ review

Perfect — appreciate the quick plan. A couple clarifications before tomorrow's call: 
- For backups: can you confirm whether multi-region replication is enabled by default and whether backups for EU customers (if any) are stored outside EU? (we only need the default behavior)
- For KMS: a high level statement of who has custodian privileges (engineering ops team vs. external provider) is sufficient; if you can include last-rotation month/year that helps. Redaction is fine.
- Subprocessor CSV: we'll need the ISO country code column for residency mapping (e.g., US, GB, DE). If you can include that column, great.

10:00 PT tomorrow works. We'll join via the invite you send. No NDA required for these artifacts — thanks for confirming.

Best,
Natalie Brooks
Sr. Vendor Risk Analyst
Cairn Health
